groupDetails.name: Pascua Florida – One of the Top Easter Events in South Tenerife
groupDetails.desc: The Pascua Florida festival in Guía de Isora is one of the most emblematic cultural events of Holy Week in southern Tenerife . Every year, the historic center of this town is transformed into a spectacular open-air museum where floral art, tradition, and creativity come together to offer a unique experience in the Canary Islands. During Holy Thursday and Easter Sunday, the streets of Guía de Isora are transformed into an artistic procession featuring stunning floral creations crafted by florists and artists. These works reinterpret the Passion of Christ through ephemeral compositions that combine color, symbolism, and design. The Easter Flower Festival in Guía de Isora is a benchmark for cultural tourism in Tenerife . Each floral arrangement is unique and unrepeatable , making this event one of the most singular cultural experiences on the island during Holy Week. Visiting the Easter celebrations in Guía de Isora means discovering a tradition that blends art, spirituality, and historical heritage in the heart of southern Tenerife. It's an event that surprises, moves, and attracts visitors each year who seek to experience Holy Week in Tenerife from an artistic and unique perspective.

groupDetails.name: Mount Teide Half Day Tour
groupDetails.desc:
On this half-day excursion youll have the opportunity to explore the largest and oldest National Park in the Canary Islands and return to your hotel to enjoy the rest of the day.

 

Youll enjoy a journey from the coast to the highest point in Tenerife, passing through Canary pine forests and traditional villages such as Vilafor.

 

As we continue along the path, well venture into volcanoes and rivers of petrified lava. Well make a few stops so you can admire one of the worlds largest calderas: Las Cañadas del Teide.

Well visit Los Roques de García at the foot of Spains highest peak: Mount Teide, at 3,718 meters above sea level. This imposing volcano, located in the heart of Tenerife, is the main reason why Teide National Park, declared in 1954, is the most visited national park in Europe.

This excursion does not include the option of riding the Teide cable car or visiting its base.

Finally, we will resume our hike and continue admiring everything this incredible natural space has to offer on the way back.

groupDetails.name: Teide Masca (Grand Tour)
groupDetails.desc:
On this tour we will spend a full day touring the most representative places in the north of Tenerife.

Our first visit will be to the Teide National Park, located in the heart of Tenerife and home to the highest peak in Spain: the volcano El Teide. Here we will stop for about 30 minutes to admire the impressive volcanic landscapes of Las Cañadas del Teide, not forgetting the emblematic Roques de García.

After this visit, we will descend to Icod de los Vinos where we will have the opportunity to contemplate the famous Drago Milenario, which is said to be more than 800 years old. You will have free time to have lunch on your own or enjoy the Canarian gastronomy tasting one of the menus that we recommend in some of the restaurants in the area.

The next destination is Garachico, a colourful coastal village with a history marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. Here we will stroll through the streets of its historic quarter, recognised as a Cultural Heritage Site and one of the most representative of the Canary Islands, and discover emblematic sites such as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by lava flows, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that defended the town from pirate attacks.

We will follow the route and enter the vibrant nature of the Teno Rural Park until we reach the hamlet of Masca, located between impressive valleys and ravines. Let yourself be surprised by the charm of the traditional architecture of this enclave, declared a Site of Ethnographic and Historical Interest and an Asset of Cultural Interest.

Flavors and Wines of Tenerife: A Journey for the Senses

On this excursion through southern Tenerife, you will discover the island's most authentic flavors and renowned wines, with the convenience of returning to your accommodation in time to continue enjoying your day.

We will start with a visit to Finca Las Margaritas, where you will learn about traditional banana cultivation and taste products made with gofio, palm honey, and tropical fruits.

After this experience, we will return so you can make the most of the rest of your day.

groupDetails.whygo: La Gomera, considered as a "virgin island" for mass tourism, has the Garajonay National Park declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. It is also the only place in the world where an authentic whistling language was developed, using only the mouth and fingers. That is why the Silbo Gomero has also been declared a World Heritage Site.

groupDetails.name: La Gomera
groupDetails.desc:
Would you like to discover the island of La Gomera on a single day trip from Tenerife? Then this is your perfect option!

Our day starts by heading to the port of Los Cristianos, where we will take a ferry to the island. Once here, we'll board the bus and head into the Hermigua Valley, where we'll have the opportunity to capture some photos of the breathtaking scenery.

We will continue the excursion until we reach the municipality of Agulo, where we will enjoy a delicious lunch in a typical restaurant with local products. If availability permits, during lunch we will witness a live demonstration of "silbo gomero", a unique language declared Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO.

After lunch we will enter the Garajonay National Park, a paradise of laurel forests and a nature reserve also declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Laguna Grande we will learn all the curiosities of this magical place where it is said that the witches of the island used to meet.

We will make a stop at the imposing Roque de Agando, one of the most emblematic places of La Gomera. Finally, we will arrive in San Sebastián, the capital of the island. Here we will have the opportunity to discover the last traces left by Christopher Columbus after his passage through La Gomera, such as the Torre del Conde or the Casa Colón. Once we have finished our visit of San Sebastian, we will head back to the ferry to Tenerife.

groupDetails.name: Island Tour + Masca
groupDetails.desc:
This excursion gives you the opportunity to get to know the essence of Tenerife in just one day.

We will start the day by visiting Candelaria. This coastal town is home to the Basilica of Candelaria, one of the most important places of worship in Tenerife. On the seashore you can admire the imposing bronze statues commemorating the ancient Guanche Kings of Tenerife.

The excursion continues in the Historic-Artistic Site of La Villa de La Orotava. The cobbled streets of its historic quarter will take us to places full of charm and culture such as La Casa de Los Balcones, the Town Hall Square or the Church of Nuestra Señora de La Concepción.

We will continue our journey through the north of Tenerife until we reach Garachico, a charming coastal town, whose history is marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. We will stroll through its historic centre, declared a Site of Cultural Interest, and visit such emblematic places as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by volcanic lava, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that protected the town from pirate attacks.

Here you will have free time to have lunch on your own or taste the Canarian gastronomy in one of the restaurants we recommend.

After this visit, we will enter the Teno Rural Park where we will enjoy its impressive natural landscapes. Its winding roads will take us to Masca, a hamlet surrounded by spectacular cliffs that preserves its traditional Canarian architecture.

groupDetails.desc:
This excursion perfectly blends history, culture, and nature. Discover Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Anaga, and San Cristóbal de La Laguna: three must-see gems in the north of Tenerife.

Our first stop will be in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, the capital of the island. We will stroll through its vibrant streets, leading us to its most iconic spots, such as Plaza de España, Plaza Weyler, or the Mercado de Nuestra Señora de África.

Next, we will venture into the Anaga massif, an impressive natural area declared a Biosphere Reserve by UNESCO in 2015 due to its extraordinary biodiversity. Here, you can enjoy some of its most representative viewpoints, like the Mirador de la Jardina or the Mirador Cruz del Carmen, offering spectacular views of the island.

Finally, we will continue to San Cristóbal de La Laguna, the first city founded in Tenerife after its conquest and a historic gem declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1999. We will walk through its historic and culturally rich streets, discovering its most significant monuments, such as the Cathedral of San Cristóbal de La Laguna or Plaza del Adelantado.

You will have time to enjoy lunch and taste the delicious Canarian cuisine in one of the charming restaurants in the city.

After a day of discovering several of Tenerife's treasures, we will return to the pickup points.

We will continue our journey into the Anaga mountain range, a stunning natural area declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015 due to its extraordinary biodiversity. Here, we will visit some of its most iconic viewpoints, such as the Mirador de la Jardina and the Mirador Cruz del Carmen.

After a day exploring some of Tenerife's treasures, we will return to the pickup points.

groupDetails.name: Puerto de la Cruz at your Leisure
groupDetails.desc:
Discover with us the charming town of Puerto de la Cruz, located in the coastal area of the Orotava Valley, in the north of Tenerife. You will have the whole day at your leisure to enjoy a pleasant day by the sea and discover all that this town has to offer.

Despite its popularity with travellers who visit the island every year, Puerto de la Cruz has not lost its seaside charm. You can stroll through its beautiful streets and squares, such as the Plaza del Charco or the Muelle Viejo.

Many people believe that one of the most outstanding attractions of the municipality is its mild climate that is maintained throughout the year, a fact that was described by several European naturalists who visited Puerto de la Cruz in the 18th and 19th centuries.

You will have the opportunity to walk around the city and discover such emblematic places as the Botanical Gardens or the spectacular Martiánez Lake, and end the day watching the waves break on the coast of San Telmo.

groupDetails.name: La Gomera Vip
groupDetails.desc:
Embark on an unforgettable adventure and dive into the essence of La Gomera, the hidden gem of the Canary Islands. In a small group of maximum 18 people, you’ll explore spectacular landscapes, ancient forests, and picturesque villages that preserve the island’s most authentic character.

From San Sebastián de La Gomera, a town full of history and charm, to the stunning viewpoints of Roque de Agando and Valle Gran Rey, every corner of the island will amaze you with its natural beauty. Enter the Garajonay National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the laurel forest wraps the landscape in a magical and mysterious atmosphere. You'll visit Chipude and El Cercado, known for their pottery tradition, and have the chance to discover the Silbo Gomero, a unique whistled language recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

During the tour, you’ll enjoy the peaceful charm of small towns like Igualero, the highest village on the island, and immerse yourself in the history and culture of this Canarian jewel. You’ll also have the option to taste the island’s delicious cuisine, with typical products such as almogrote, gofio, and palm honey.

This excursion includes everything you need for a carefree experience: an official Canary Islands guide, ferry tickets, and comfortable transport in an air-conditioned bus. Just relax and let yourself be swept away by the magic of La Gomera.

Don’t miss the chance to discover this fascinating island in an exclusive and personal way. Book now and get ready for a journey you’ll never forget.

groupDetails.name: Gran Canaria Experience
groupDetails.desc:
We will travel by ferry from Tenerife to Gran Canaria in the most comfortable and fastest way with Fred Olsen Express.

Arriving at Puerto de las Nieves in Agaete, we will head straight to the historic quarter of Vegueta, where we will take a walking tour through its streets full of culture and history.

After exploring Vegueta, we'll head to the Poema del Mar aquarium in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. This impressive theme park, which opened on 17 December 2017, will immerse us in the majesty of nature in three incomparable environments: jungle, beach reef and deep ocean. The 12,000-square-metre facility features 35 marine and river ecosystems from around the globe.  The aquarium pays tribute, with its name and architectural lines, to the Canarian artist Néstor de la Torre, who stood out in the avant-garde of the early 20th century, and his work "Poemas del Atlántico" (Poems of the Atlantic). Here we can admire the largest curved glass in the world (a methacrylate weighing 140 tons, 36 metres long and 7 metres high), which exhibits some 350 species from 35 different ecosystems, from sharks, piranhas, freshwater rays, crocodiles and sea dragons.

Our last stop will be the Arehucas distilleries, where we will learn the secret of the uniqueness of its rums, a journey through the history, tradition and know-how of Arehucas. During the visit we will explore one of the oldest rum cellars in Europe, made up of 4,308 American oak casks, some even signed by famous personalities. Here we will be explained the process of elaboration of this drink, and we will enjoy a tasting of rums and liqueurs to end the day with a good taste in our mouths.

After this experience, we will return to Puerto de las Nieves in Agaete to take the ferry back to Tenerife.

Experiencing the island of La Palma to the fullest is possible with this day trip from Tenerife, perfect for those who wish to discover the landscapes, history, and volcanic impact of this gem in the Canary archipelago. The activity begins upon arrival in Santa Cruz de La Palma, where a guided tour takes visitors through its charming historic center, considered one of the most beautiful and best-preserved in the Canaries. During the walk, participants visit the local market La Recova and admire the famous colonial-style balconies that define the city’s traditional architecture.

The itinerary continues with a stop at the Mirador de La Cumbrecita, located in the Caldera de Taburiente National Park, a stunning natural setting with unique views of La Palma’s mountainous heart.

Next, the tour heads to the ground zero of the Tajogaite volcano, following the newly built road across the solidified lava flows. From here, travelers witness striking views of Todoque and the homes destroyed by the eruption—a powerful and moving experience that reflects the magnitude of nature's force.

Free time is included, allowing each traveler to explore at their own pace, shop, or enjoy local cuisine at one of the nearby restaurants. Meals are not included, offering more flexibility and making the most of the time on the island.

An ideal choice for those seeking a day excursion from Tenerife to La Palma, combining history, natural beauty, and recent volcanic activity in one unforgettable experience.

This is a perfect excursion for astronomy lovers.

You will start the tour at the Teide Observatory, where you will do a guided tour. There, your Starlight guide (specialist in the observation of the night sky) will explain the importance of the Canary sky, the telescopes of the observatory and the different projects of the Astrophysics Institute of the Canary Islands. You will also enjoy the sun as never before, since you can observe its spots and flares through the telescope.

You will see the sunset from the Observatory, a unique spectacle in which the sun hides behind El Teide. A range of colors will adorn the views of the volcano and the ocean.

Then we will go to the base of the Teide's Cable Car and, far from the light pollution of urban areas, you will discover the secrets of the sky in an astronomical observation with the naked eye and with a long-range telescope. Did you know that from El Teide you can see 83 of the 88 constellations officially recognized?

You will discover stars, planets, galaxies and clusters as you have never imagined, while your Starlight guide teaches you the constellations, the celestial map and provides you with interesting information about the objects you observe. Marvel at the immensity of the universe and live an experience without equal, in one of the most visited national parks in the world.

It also includes a stop for a meal. You choose whether you prefer to bring your own food, use the Cable Car’s vending machines or buy the optional picnic along with your ‘Astronomic Tour including a visit of Teide Observatory’.

Discover the Teide National Park like never before: under the starry blanket of night. This nocturnal excursion will take you to explore the beauty of Teide at dusk, when the landscape is transformed and the sky reveals 83 of the 88 known constellations.

During the ascent, you will cross different ecosystems, from rural areas and forests to high mountain scrubland, home to native plants such as broom and summit rosebush. You will also see small bats, harmless companions of the night, which live in the volcanic tunnels of the park. These tunnels are also home to unique creatures adapted to total darkness, many of them exclusive to this environment.

Teide's sky is one of the best on the planet for stargazing. The scarce light pollution of the environment gives you a clear, sharp sky dome full of mythological stories and mysteries, which you can discover in full with the help of the Starlight guides, who will be at your disposal throughout the observation. This will take place at the cable car base station, at an altitude of 2,356 metres, with professional long-range telescopes. Among volcanoes, with the colours of a natural treasure such as this wild enclave and with the nerves of being about to discover planets, galaxies, clusters and -if there is a full moon- a whole lunar geography that will make you dream.

A unique experience that combines the magic of nature and astronomy in a spectacular setting.

groupDetails.name: Tenerife Stars
groupDetails.desc:
If you are an astronomy lover or are looking for a unique experience, a visit to Teide in Tenerife is a must. The island is known for its stunning natural beauty and clear skies, making it an ideal place for stargazing. At 3,718 metres high, Mount Teide is the highest point in Spain and offers spectacular views of the night sky.

The Teide National Park tour offers the opportunity to enjoy a spectacular sunset and an unforgettable astronomical experience. Departures are from various points in Costa Adeje, Playa de las Americas and Los Cristianos. Along the way, you can admire the breathtaking landscapes of the island and witness a sunset that paints the sky with an incredible variety of colours.

The route continues up to an altitude of 2,000 metres, where the real magic begins. The Teide National Park, free of light pollution and certified as a Starlight destination, allows you to enjoy clear, crisp views of the starry sky, offering the opportunity to observe shooting stars like never before.

To enhance the experience, powerful lasers are used to point out constellations, important stars and astronomical navigation techniques. With the use of powerful telescopes, you can observe the surface of the moon (when visible), planets, nebulae, star clusters and, under optimal conditions, the Andromeda galaxy. During certain times of the year, the Milky Way can also be photographed using a mobile phone through the telescope.

At the end of the tour, you will return to your starting point, taking with you unforgettable memories of this unique experience.

groupDetails.name: Banana Experience
groupDetails.desc:
Finca Las Margaritas is based on extensive volcanic wasteland that since 3 or 4 million years ago covered the coastal platform of Las Galletas. In this large agricultural area of 825 Ha is located the largest bananas plantations in greenhouse of Tenerife, where moves a volume of more than 26 thousand tons for export anually.

FINCA LAS MARGARITAS began with the cultivation of banana in Las Galletas in the year 1977, the union and several family members of Adolfo Guerra González entrepreneurship and Margarita Hernández Pérez, later named the estate, being 86 years old in 2012. Both came from a long family generation of farmers in S/C de La Palma and San Andrés y Sauces.

On this farm are produces 2 cultivars of Canary Island banana, the great dwarf and the thick Palm or small dwarf, the Dwarf Cavendish variety, reaching an average of 45-50 klg per bunch, and can find copies that they exceed the 70 klg. The acreage is of approximately 7 Ha with 98% of bananas and 2% of fruit trees such as: mango, papaya and avocado.

groupDetails.name: Pirámides de Güímar
groupDetails.desc:
The Ethnographic Park & Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar is a large open-air museum and one of the five official botanical gardens of the Canary Islands. The Park was founded in 1998 by the renowned Norwegian researcher Thor Heyerdahl, who was responsible for safeguarding the pyramids from an urban development plan.

In addition to the pyramids, the Park includes four outdoor trails and specialised gardens, spread over more than 64,000m2. The routes allow visitors to stroll freely through the extensive gardens, discovering interesting aspects of Canarian culture and nature. These routes include a Canarian Botanical Route, a Cultural Route and a Volcanic Route. The facilities also include the Casa Chacona Museum and an Auditorium. 

As for its botanical collections, you can visit the Poison Garden, unique in Spain, and the Sustainable Garden, a reproduction of a Canarian ravine, including a watercourse and presenting the flora characteristic of these environments in a sustainable way. The Tropicarium shows the life strategies used by orchids and insectivorous plants to survive in tropical conditions.

The Park was the winner of the 'Best Overall Sustainable Tourism Practice 2021' award for the island of Tenerife and a national finalist in the 'Remarkable Venue Awards 2022' in the Best Hidden Gem category, which highlights the most outstanding and special places for travellers from all over the world. The Park has also been awarded the Biosphere Committed distinction for its sustainable commitment and is a member of the Climate Heritage Network.

The Ethnographic Park & Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar offers a unique outdoor experience, without crowds of people thanks to its 30,000m2 of accessible garden areas, allowing culture and nature lovers to enjoy a day outdoors in a different, safe and sustainable environment.

San Blas Reserve is an open-air museum, where you can explore archaeological sites, ancient caves, and historical remains that reveal what life was like on the island centuries ago.

More than 4 million years ago, lava flows shaped this unique volcanic landscape, later sculpted by wind and water into what is now known as the breathtaking “lunar landscape” of San Blas.

The visit includes access to an innovative Interpretation Center, equipped with advanced interactive rooms and immersive audiovisual experiences. Here, you will discover the secrets of San Blas' geology, biodiversity, and history in a fun and educational way.

Immerse yourself in a journey where nature, history, and technology come together to create an unforgettable adventure in the heart of Tenerife’s volcanic landscape.

Discover Loro Parque: A Sanctuary of Life and Conservation
Visit Loro Parque, a natural paradise that is home to more than 400 animal species in a unique environment designed for their well-being and conservation. Considered one of the most respected zoos in the world, this park in Tenerife is much more than a tourist attraction: it is a true refuge for biodiversity.
Every corner of the park reflects a genuine commitment to love, respect, and care for each animal, with personalized plans that follow the most advanced veterinary and biological knowledge. Here, you will learn about endangered species, discover fascinating facts about wildlife, and connect with nature like never before.
Explore lush gardens, enjoy unforgettable experiences with your loved ones, and be inspired by a global mission: protecting our planet.
Loro Parque is not just a place to visit, it is a place to live.
Buy your tickets now and be a part of conservation!

groupDetails.desc:
Siam Park has been named, for the seventh consecutive year, the best water park in the world by TripAdvisor users.

A place full of different environments in which the vegetation catches you and every corner is a source of emotion, where both the little ones and the older ones will find a perfect space for the "Siam experience" to be unforgettable.

The little ones will be able to enjoy Coco Beach, a water park within the water park itself, and they will become true adventurers enjoying exciting attractions such as Bodhi Trail, Sawasdee or The Lost City, while those seeking tranquility will be able to enjoy the 13,000m2 from Siam beach, a white sand beach in the Algarve, and the birth of its waves at Wave Palace.

For adrenaline lovers, the thrill is guaranteed with Tower of Power, the impressive 28-meter high slide whose route ends under a marine exhibition with fish, rays and sharks, or Singha, the fastest water roller coaster in the world, with almost 250 meters of frenetic travel, extreme speed corners and 14 changes of direction that defy the laws of physics.

To complete the experience, the park has perfect spaces for all kinds of needs where you can unleash unknown sensations, several establishments where you can eat and recharge your batteries with a gastronomic selection where you can find a wide variety of organic dishes.

In addition, to enjoy exclusively, Siam Park has VIP Houses and private Villas equipped with all the luxury of details to make your experience unforgettable.

groupDetails.willDo: In the castle of Count Don Rodrigo you will witness an authentic knights equestrian tournament, while having a feast in medieval style.
groupDetails.canDesc: Free cancellation up to 48 hours before the activity. If you cancel within 48 hours of the activity, 50% will be charged.
groupDetails.name: Medieval Show
groupDetails.desc:
The San Miguel Castle is an impressive construction of 6,000 square metres and made of Canarian canto stone, with principal towers of more than 16 metres in height and an extensive area of 20,000 square metres .From the moment you enter the grounds, you find yourself in an authentic medieval world.

The entrance is decorated with historical armour, swords, chests and scrolls of the medieval epoch. The Count, Don Rodrigo, and his daughter, the young Countess, will greet you and welcome you to their Castle. The kind subjects of Count Rodrigo will guide you to the Tournament Hall, where the complex show of medieval fights and games will take placein the presence of the Counts in their Royal box seats.

During the Tournament, you will be served the banquet just as it was done in medieval times; The soup is drunk and an entire chicken per person with its garnish is eaten by hand.The dinner is completed with dessert and beverages.

The Count´s guests are seated in stands of long tables and benches where the visibility is optimal from anywhere in the Tournament Hall. The sand arena where the horses and knights will perform is of 50 metres in long.

The Hall has a capacity of 1100 guests.Usually after the Tournaments, the guests move to adjourn to a second hall which has a capacity for 800 guests.

The Ballroom, as Count Rodrigo calls it, has a large stage where the guests can dance, where any type of performance can be arranged: Orchestra, Comedians, Acrobatics, Spanish Ballet, etc.

Auditorio Pirámide de Arona presents "History," a unique musical spectacle that brings to life the most memorable moments in the history of music, performed live by 30 talented artists from 15 different countries.

This captivating journey through time pays homage to the greatest artists and composers of the world, from Mozart to Michael Jackson, including iconic figures such as Beethoven, Caruso, Elvis, The Beatles, Queen, Abba, and Pink Floyd, among others.

With stunning audiovisual production and spectacular costumes, attendees are transported through the eras that have shaped the soundtrack of our lives, from the Middle Ages to the present day, encompassing the Renaissance, the Roaring Twenties, Silent Cinema, Soul, Gospel, Rock, and much more.

In addition to recreating the best classic and contemporary choreographies, "History" performs live renditions of the most beautiful film and theater soundtracks, while also celebrating the wonderful musicals of Broadway.

This live music, dance, theater, and acrobatics show is suitable for all ages and nationalities, offering an unforgettable experience for all who attend. Join us on this journey through the history of music!

groupDetails.name: Banana Experience
groupDetails.desc:
Finca Las Margaritas is based on extensive volcanic wasteland that since 3 or 4 million years ago covered the coastal platform of Las Galletas. In this large agricultural area of 825 Ha is located the largest bananas plantations in greenhouse of Tenerife, where moves a volume of more than 26 thousand tons for export anually.

FINCA LAS MARGARITAS began with the cultivation of banana in Las Galletas in the year 1977, the union and several family members of Adolfo Guerra González entrepreneurship and Margarita Hernández Pérez, later named the estate, being 86 years old in 2012. Both came from a long family generation of farmers in S/C de La Palma and San Andrés y Sauces.

On this farm are produces 2 cultivars of Canary Island banana, the great dwarf and the thick Palm or small dwarf, the Dwarf Cavendish variety, reaching an average of 45-50 klg per bunch, and can find copies that they exceed the 70 klg. The acreage is of approximately 7 Ha with 98% of bananas and 2% of fruit trees such as: mango, papaya and avocado.

groupDetails.name: Pirámides de Güímar
groupDetails.desc:
The Ethnographic Park & Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar is a large open-air museum and one of the five official botanical gardens of the Canary Islands. The Park was founded in 1998 by the renowned Norwegian researcher Thor Heyerdahl, who was responsible for safeguarding the pyramids from an urban development plan.

In addition to the pyramids, the Park includes four outdoor trails and specialised gardens, spread over more than 64,000m2. The routes allow visitors to stroll freely through the extensive gardens, discovering interesting aspects of Canarian culture and nature. These routes include a Canarian Botanical Route, a Cultural Route and a Volcanic Route. The facilities also include the Casa Chacona Museum and an Auditorium. 

As for its botanical collections, you can visit the Poison Garden, unique in Spain, and the Sustainable Garden, a reproduction of a Canarian ravine, including a watercourse and presenting the flora characteristic of these environments in a sustainable way. The Tropicarium shows the life strategies used by orchids and insectivorous plants to survive in tropical conditions.

The Park was the winner of the 'Best Overall Sustainable Tourism Practice 2021' award for the island of Tenerife and a national finalist in the 'Remarkable Venue Awards 2022' in the Best Hidden Gem category, which highlights the most outstanding and special places for travellers from all over the world. The Park has also been awarded the Biosphere Committed distinction for its sustainable commitment and is a member of the Climate Heritage Network.

The Ethnographic Park & Botanical Garden Pirámides de Güímar offers a unique outdoor experience, without crowds of people thanks to its 30,000m2 of accessible garden areas, allowing culture and nature lovers to enjoy a day outdoors in a different, safe and sustainable environment.

San Blas Reserve is an open-air museum, where you can explore archaeological sites, ancient caves, and historical remains that reveal what life was like on the island centuries ago.

More than 4 million years ago, lava flows shaped this unique volcanic landscape, later sculpted by wind and water into what is now known as the breathtaking “lunar landscape” of San Blas.

The visit includes access to an innovative Interpretation Center, equipped with advanced interactive rooms and immersive audiovisual experiences. Here, you will discover the secrets of San Blas' geology, biodiversity, and history in a fun and educational way.

Immerse yourself in a journey where nature, history, and technology come together to create an unforgettable adventure in the heart of Tenerife’s volcanic landscape.

Book now and uncover one of Tenerife’s best-kept secrets!

In this "nature classroom" located in Icod de Los Vinos you will find ethnographic areas of special interest such as a medicinal garden with plants used by the island's ancestors as natural remedies. A "carbonera", which was the traditional way of obtaining charcoal and which was a very important resource on the island. A wine press, or a cave where you can admire the representation of an aboriginal burial. And the star of the place: the spectacular Millenian Dragon Tree, the longest living tree of its species and a national monument since 1917.

The posthumous work of the famous artist César Manrique from Lanzarote, the Parque Marítimo de Santa Cruz de Tenerife was inaugurated in 1995 and has become a symbol of the capital, forming part of the city's landscape.
In addition to its 3 salt water swimming pools, it has restaurant services, shops, changing rooms, showers and gymnasium as well as sun lounger and parasol rental services, making it an ideal place for tourist, family, leisure and relaxation activities.

groupDetails.willDo: The Teide Cable Car will take you up a few meters from the peak of the highest point in Spain. Enjoy the immensity of the landscape.
groupDetails.canDesc: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before the excursion. If you cancel within 24 hours of the excursion, there will not be a refund.
groupDetails.name: El Teide Cable Car
groupDetails.desc:
For the Guanches, the aboriginal Canary Islanders, Mount Teide was a volcano considered sacred since ancient times, like Mount Fuji, Mount Olympus or Mount Kilimanjaro. This visit to Pico del Teide by cable car allows you to contemplate the landscape of the largest National Park in the Canary Islands from a height of 3555 metres above sea level.

Its particular climate, altitude and volcanic forms invite you to contemplate and enjoy a unique moment that you will remember for the rest of your life. A visit to the Teide volcano is always different, the effects of the light throughout the day and the seasons with their climatic changes give the landscape an ever new appearance. However, two sensations remain constant: the immensity of the landscape and the magnificent silence.

The Teide Volcano is at its most emblematic at sunrise and sunset. The spectacular nature of these moments is marked by the different tones of the sky and the light reflected on the rocks.

If you want to go up to the Teide cable car you must select "Cable car for excursion" in our excursion Teide National Park.

groupDetails.name: Medieval Show
groupDetails.desc:
The San Miguel Castle is an impressive construction of 6,000 square metres and made of Canarian canto stone, with principal towers of more than 16 metres in height and an extensive area of 20,000 square metres .From the moment you enter the grounds, you find yourself in an authentic medieval world.

The entrance is decorated with historical armour, swords, chests and scrolls of the medieval epoch. The Count, Don Rodrigo, and his daughter, the young Countess, will greet you and welcome you to their Castle. The kind subjects of Count Rodrigo will guide you to the Tournament Hall, where the complex show of medieval fights and games will take placein the presence of the Counts in their Royal box seats.

During the Tournament, you will be served the banquet just as it was done in medieval times; The soup is drunk and an entire chicken per person with its garnish is eaten by hand.The dinner is completed with dessert and beverages.

The Count´s guests are seated in stands of long tables and benches where the visibility is optimal from anywhere in the Tournament Hall. The sand arena where the horses and knights will perform is of 50 metres in long.

The Hall has a capacity of 1100 guests.Usually after the Tournaments, the guests move to adjourn to a second hall which has a capacity for 800 guests.

The Ballroom, as Count Rodrigo calls it, has a large stage where the guests can dance, where any type of performance can be arranged: Orchestra, Comedians, Acrobatics, Spanish Ballet, etc.

Auditorio Pirámide de Arona presents "History," a unique musical spectacle that brings to life the most memorable moments in the history of music, performed live by 30 talented artists from 15 different countries.

This captivating journey through time pays homage to the greatest artists and composers of the world, from Mozart to Michael Jackson, including iconic figures such as Beethoven, Caruso, Elvis, The Beatles, Queen, Abba, and Pink Floyd, among others.

With stunning audiovisual production and spectacular costumes, attendees are transported through the eras that have shaped the soundtrack of our lives, from the Middle Ages to the present day, encompassing the Renaissance, the Roaring Twenties, Silent Cinema, Soul, Gospel, Rock, and much more.

In addition to recreating the best classic and contemporary choreographies, "History" performs live renditions of the most beautiful film and theater soundtracks, while also celebrating the wonderful musicals of Broadway.

This live music, dance, theater, and acrobatics show is suitable for all ages and nationalities, offering an unforgettable experience for all who attend. Join us on this journey through the history of music!

Sail aboard Freebird Catamaran and experience a unique adventure in Tenerife, where you can immerse yourself in nature and relax under the sun while watching whales and dolphins in their natural habitat. Learn about their habits, discover how they feed, and explore one of the world's top destinations for observing these incredible creatures.

Book a 3-hour excursion around the Costa Adeje area, or opt for a more complete 4.5-hour experience that will take you to the breathtaking cliffs of Los Gigantes and Masca.

After the whale and dolphin watching, you can unwind and enjoy a refreshing swim in the sea.

Freebird Catamaran, a member of the Charter for Sustainability in Whale Watching by Turismo de Tenerife, ensures a responsible and respectful approach to the well-being of whales, dolphins, and their marine environment.

Make your trip to Tenerife an unforgettable sea adventure.

groupDetails.desc:
Live the experience on board an authentic oriental sailboat, completely constructed in teak hard wood, for the private use of an Arabian Sheikh.

Shogun has 2 levels, 3 services available (for wich one is adapted for the disabled people), an open bar, a large central table where your meal it will be served.
A 5 hour trip, during of which we will see pilot whales and bottlenose dolphins, an internationally species.

The SHOGUN complies with these rules and holds a yellow flag with a blue boat badge that guarantees the sight seeing of the whales and dolphins with their maximum welfare involved.

With its geografical position and subject to the action of the Trade Winds and Teide´s summit acting as a back drop, the Canary Islands and mainly the south of Tenerife counts on a water temperature of between 17-24 degrees during the whole year.

This ensures the permanent presence of many species of cetaceans eg pilot whales bottlenose dolphins along with other migratory species eg Finwhales, spermwhales, common dolphins...

After this emotional viewing of these marvellous animals we will anchor in the Bay of Masca, and the impressive cliffs of Los Gigantes to enjoy a well deserved swim and hearty lunch.

Bat4All is an exceptional and inclusive boat, designed to offer an accessible sailing experience for everyone, including people with reduced mobility. This barrier-free boat can accommodate up to 10 people and 4 wheelchairs, guaranteeing comfort and personalisation.

Start your journey in the spacious aft cockpit or relax on the comfortable bow cushions. The upper deck, with ample seating and a sun deck with artificial grass, is ideal for whale watching. The hydraulic platform allows safe access to the sea, even for people with reduced mobility, offering a unique experience with the sea creatures.

The qualified crew will guide you through the nature reserve, introducing you to sea turtles, dolphins and whales. Snorkelling equipment is provided to explore beneath the surface, and when you return, a delicious cold Italian pasta awaits you.

The bathroom is wheelchair accessible and the crew offers assistance in the sea, ensuring that everyone can swim and snorkel. We will anchor in a serene bay with warm waters (20/22 degrees all year round). With a large sun deck for whale watching, relaxing and sunbathing, Bat4All is perfect for families and private events.

Teide Tour 4hrDiscover the mid- and high-mountain areas and the most visited place in Spain... "El Teide." Duration: 4 hrs. Requirements: 18 years of age and drivers license. Elevation: 2,400 m. The adventure will start in Puerto de la Cruz, where the team will pick you up to take you on board the 4x4 jeep. The highlights of the excursion include the hamlet of Masca, which is extremely characteristic for the nature and antiquity of its buildings. You will also visit places like Garachico, the village that rose from the ashes after being devastated by a volcano more than 300 years ago, the charming village of Icod de los Vinos with the ancient dragon tree, or Santiago del Teide. You will stop for lunch at a restaurant in El Tanque where you will be able to taste the Canarian gastronomy surrounded by camels and when you complete the tour we will take you comfortably back to the pick up point.

groupDetails.name: Jeep Safari Teide Masca
groupDetails.desc:
There are countless attractions on the island of Tenerife, but if we had to choose just a few, it would be the ones you will find on this excursion. Not only does it include a visit to some of the most remarkable and peculiar spots in the Teide National Park, declared a World Heritage Site, but also to a small village with very traditional and typical buildings: Masca.

On the route, which starts in Playa de las Américas, you will pass through villages as unique as Vilaflor, where for centuries they have known what it is like to live next to a dormant volcano. You will stop at viewpoints to contemplate the marvellous views of the island, we will go to the Pico Viejo volcano (inactive, with a crater of 800 metres in diameter full of colours) and you will also stroll through the little streets of Masca, a beautiful village that still preserves buildings from the 18th century. 

During the tour we will stop for lunch in a local restaurant where you can order a menu and enjoy the authentic Canarian gastronomy in the best possible place. On board of our 4x4 jeep you will discover the Cañadas del Teide National Park, which is the most visited in Spain. In addition, you will visit the most typical villages of the area. Throughout this route, which lasts 7 hours, you will witness the most peculiar corners of the island's geography, such as the village of Vilaflor, which is the highest in Spain, or Masca and its typical farmhouses. At each stop there will be a person who will inform you punctually about the places you are visiting, so you won't miss any of the exciting stories and incredible details.

Decide to discover the wild side of the island of Tenerife by Jeep!

groups.name: Ascent to the Peak of Mount Teide + Cable Car

groupDetails.faq:
Included:

A special permit from the National Park for the trail to the peak of Mt. Teide.

A Spanish or English-speaking guide who will reveal all of the volcano’s secrets to you.

Teide Cable Car return ticket.

Not included:

Food and drinks.

Guide in other language than Spanish or English.

Important Information:


	Please be aware that we cannot confirm your VIP hike to Teide and cable car package reservation until we have issued named access passes to the crater for each member of your group. 
	It is necessary to present your ID or passport at the point of access to the trail leading to the crater.
	In the event that the path to the peak is closed, Teide National Park staff may permit access only to mountaineers belonging to a federation who can provide sufficient proof of their ability, and who are appropriately equipped (with mountain-climbing equipment—in particular boots, crampons and an ice-axe). It is the individual’s responsibility to ensure that they possess the appropriate documentation and equipment, therefore the absence of either exempts Volcano Teide from any liability.


RESTRICTIONS


	Children under 6, pregnant women and people with heart problems are not allowed to participate in this Mount Teide tour with Cable Car due to the risk that high altitude poses to their health.
	The Teide Peak Tour with Cable Car is not recommended for people with reduced mobility or injuries.
	If you have health problems, you should consult with your doctor before undertaking this hike.
	In accordance with current regulations, persons with any physical disability or motor impairment are not permitted to make the ascent by cable car, because of the potential risks if the vehicle has to be evacuated.
	It is essential to bear in mind that in the event of the failure of the cable car system due to unexpected technical reasons, passengers already at the upper station will have to make their descent on foot and using steep mountain paths.
	Pets are not allowed.
	Suitcases and large bags are not permitted.


Important: Access to the cable car may be restricted if you are not wearing appropriate footwear, so it is recommended that you wear sports or hiking shoes. For safety reasons, access in flip-flops or flip-flops, footwear without back support, heels, wedges or open shoes with smooth soles is expressly prohibited.

Changes and cancellations: 

If weather conditions mean that the cable car is not operating when the ‘Climbing the Teide Crater with the help of the Cable Car’ excursion is due to take place, a visit to the National Park with an alternative trail will be held instead. Customers will be refunded the price difference between the ‘Teide Tour without Cable Car’ and the ‘Climbing to Mount Teide Crater with Cable Car’ excursions, i.e. €49 per adult and €24.50 per child shall be charged.

If the cable car is operational but the Teide National Park staff keep the trail to the summit closed, the ascent will be made by cable car to La Rambleta and an alternative hike will be carried out. In this case, the difference between the price of the Teide Tour with Cable Car and the Summit Ascent will be refunded, meaning €87 will be charged per adult and €43.50 per child.

groupDetails.desc:
This company offers unique experiences on quad bikes to discover the most authentic north of Tenerife. Their routes combine spectacular landscapes, local history, and the perfect dose of adrenaline, catering both to those seeking tranquillity and adventure lovers.

Panoramic Route
A 100% on-road tour through the historic center of La Orotava, winding among pine forests and lava fields to viewpoints such as La Bermeja and Corral del Niño (2,300 m altitude). Includes unforgettable views of Teide, the famous sea of clouds, and a stop with a local snack and refreshing drink.

Action and Culture Route
For those seeking more thrill: a ride from Puerto de la Cruz to a virgin beach, a visit to the historic center of Los Realejos, and a 30-minute off-road circuit with several difficulty levels. It ends at the El Lance Viewpoint (800 m) with views over the La Orotava Valley and a well-deserved traditional snack with a cold drink.

Explore hidden beaches and protected natural areas near Caleta de Adeje on a Stand Up Paddle (SUP) trip. Discover secret corners while snorkelling in crystal clear waters. Ideal for those who are looking for adventure and connection with nature in Tenerife.

The activity is divided into 3 stages:

First, the team will provide you with the paddle board, life jacket and paddle, as well as an explanation of the places you will visit. You will learn the safety rules and the basic notions necessary for the practice of paddle surfing, which you will practice in the water before the route. Once you have acquired the basic knowledge, the adventure begins, exploring the most beautiful landscapes of the south of Tenerife. To make the most of the experience, you will have snorkelling equipment at your disposal to explore the marine landscape of these volcanic coves.

The route of the trip will depend on the level of the group.


	Basic: Ideal for beginners, this tour focuses on teaching and practising basic snorkelling techniques. It includes a trip to the nearby beach of Los Morteros.
	Intermediate: For those with previous SUP experience. Offers a moderate challenge including visits to Los Morteros and the next beach, Diego Hernandez.
	Advanced: Intended for participants with advanced SUP skills, this is the most challenging tour. It includes a visit to Puertito de Adeje, a picturesque fishing village on the south coast of Tenerife.

groupDetails.name: El Teide Cable Car
groupDetails.desc:
For the Guanches, the aboriginal Canary Islanders, Mount Teide was a volcano considered sacred since ancient times, like Mount Fuji, Mount Olympus or Mount Kilimanjaro. This visit to Pico del Teide by cable car allows you to contemplate the landscape of the largest National Park in the Canary Islands from a height of 3555 metres above sea level.

Its particular climate, altitude and volcanic forms invite you to contemplate and enjoy a unique moment that you will remember for the rest of your life. A visit to the Teide volcano is always different, the effects of the light throughout the day and the seasons with their climatic changes give the landscape an ever new appearance. However, two sensations remain constant: the immensity of the landscape and the magnificent silence.

The Teide Volcano is at its most emblematic at sunrise and sunset. The spectacular nature of these moments is marked by the different tones of the sky and the light reflected on the rocks.

If you want to go up to the Teide cable car you must select "Cable car for excursion" in our excursion Teide National Park.

Enjoy exclusive access to witness the transformation of Teide National Park at sunset and be amazed by the starry sky, one of the purest on the planet.

In this VIP experience, you will explore the different ecosystems of the Park on a private and comfortable ascent, from rural landscapes and laurel forests to the high mountain, home to unique species such as broom and rosalillo de cumbre. Along the way, you will discover little-known natural secrets, such as volcanic tunnels that host creatures adapted to darkness and discreet native bats flying through the night.

As night falls, the sky of Teide becomes an unrivalled stage: under a crystal-clear atmosphere, free from light pollution, you will have the chance to admire 83 of the 88 known constellations, planets, clusters, and distant galaxies. All accompanied by your private Starlight guide, who will reveal myths, curiosities, and mysteries of the cosmos, while you enjoy personalised attention.

The observation will take place in a unique location, the base station of the cable car, at 2,356 metres above sea level, with professional long-range telescopes at your disposal. On full moon nights, you will discover in detail the fascinating lunar geography, as if walking on its surface.

An exclusive, intimate, and sophisticated journey that combines the best of nature, astronomy, and the pleasure of travelling in style.

groupDetails.desc:
This excursion is designed for true astronomy enthusiasts who wish to enjoy personalized attention, without rush, and in an intimate atmosphere.

You will begin the experience at the Teide Observatory, with a private guided visit in the afternoon. Your Starlight guide, an expert in night-sky observation, will explain in a close and engaging way the importance of the Canary skies, how the telescopes work, and the most outstanding projects of the Canary Islands Astrophysics Institute. You will also observe the sun as never before, discovering sunspots and flares through a specialized telescope.

Afterwards, you will enjoy a unique sunset from the Observatory itself, where the sun hides behind majestic Mount Teide and the sky is painted with colors illuminating the volcano and the ocean.

At nightfall, we will move to the base of the Teide Cable Car, far from any light pollution. There you will take part in an exclusive astronomical observation, both with the naked eye and through long-range telescopes. From this privileged spot, 83 of the 88 officially recognized constellations can be observed.

You will discover stars, planets, galaxies, and clusters as never before, while your guide teaches you to interpret the celestial map and shares with you fascinating facts about the universe. An unrepeatable experience in one of the most spectacular national parks on the planet.

groupDetails.faq:
Included: 


	Special permit from the Park for the whole group to access the Teide crater.
	A private group guide in Spanish, English or German.
	Teide Cable Car ticket for the descent.
	Transfer from the southern and northern parts of Tenerife.


Meal not included.

Important: the price includes a private tour for 2 people. If you want to add more people to your group, you must select the option ''Extra Person" and add it to the basket.
Maximum of 8 people per group.

Do not hesitate to contact us to help you organize your VIP group activity.

Restrictions:


	Children under 14, pregnant women and people with heart problems are not allowed to participate in this activity.
	The ascent to the peak on foot is not recommended for people with reduced mobility or injuries.
	People with health problems should consult with their doctors before undertaking this hike.
	In accordance with current regulations, persons with any physical disability or motor impairment are not permitted to make the ascent by cable car, because of the potential risks if the vehicle has to be evacuated.
	In the event of the failure of the cable car system due to unexpected technical reasons, passengers already at the upper station will have to make their descent on foot and using steep mountain paths.


Important information:


	Please be aware that the reservation of this activity will be pending confirmation until Volcano Teide have issued named access passes to the crater.
	In the event that Volcano Teide are unable to confirm the activity, they will offer you an alternative date or a refund of the amount paid.
	It is necessary to present your ID or passport at the point of access to the trail leading to the crater.
	In the event that the path to the peak is closed, Teide National Park staff may permit access only to mountaineers belonging to a federation who can provide sufficient proof of their ability, and who are appropriately equipped. It is the individual’s responsibility to ensure that they possess the appropriate documentation and equipment, therefore the absence of either exempts Volcano Teide from any liability.


Cancelations and changes:


	In the event that it is not possible to carry out the activity due to adverse weather conditions or the closure of one of the trails we usually walk during this hiking activity, Volcano Teide will cancel your hike to Teide and give you a refund of the amount paid.
	In case the weather conditions do not allow the operation of the cable car, the visit to the National Park will be made in an alternative hike. The difference between the price of the exclusive Teide Tour and the ascent to the VIP peak will be refunded. Up to a maximum of 2 people will be charged 115€ per person and 31€ for each additional person. The difference paid will be refunded. 
	In case the cable car is operational but the ascent path to the peak is closed, the visit to the National Park will be carried out with a cable car ascent to La Rambleta and an alternative hike. Up to a maximum of 2 people will be charged 147'50€ per person and 73€ for each additional person. The difference paid will be refunded. 
	If the cable car cannot be used to descend on the day of the activity due to adverse weather conditions, Volcano Teide will offer you two alternative options: descent on foot from the peak to the starting point of the Montaña Blanca trail or a shorter walk up to the Refuge only, without accessing the crater, and then descent on foot down the Montaña Blanca.
	In the event of the onset of poor weather conditions during the hike, the guide will decide whether to continue the ascent to the peak or cancel it.
	Cancellations are not admitted once the reservation is confirmed.

groupDetails.name: VIP Ascent to the Peak on foot
groupDetails.desc:
Your guided climb to Teide summit with your own private guide begins at Montaña Blanca at 2,320 m.

What can you expect from this route to the Teide crater?


	You’ll begin the route on paths of pumice stone and lava; a low gradient ascending walk that lasts an hour and a half.
	The path narrows and a there’s a slight incline before you reach the Altavista Refuge at 3,260 m.
	There you will take a rest to eat and let your bodies adapt to the pressure and climate.
	You will continue on paths of solidified lava until you reach the Teide Cable Car station (3,550 m).
	You will behold some spectacular views of the Teide National Park and the island of Tenerife from the cable car upper station.
	​


The climax of your epic ascent on foot to the peak of Teide with your own private guide is the final stretch to the Teide crater.

The ascent will be much harder but the reward will be worth it.

After the final effort you’ll enjoy time to relax and take in the magnificent panoramic views of the Canary Archipelago from an altitude of 3,718 m.

Embark on an unforgettable adventure and dive into the essence of La Gomera, the hidden gem of the Canary Islands. In a small group of maximum 18 people, you’ll explore spectacular landscapes, ancient forests, and picturesque villages that preserve the island’s most authentic character.

From San Sebastián de La Gomera, a town full of history and charm, to the stunning viewpoints of Roque de Agando and Valle Gran Rey, every corner of the island will amaze you with its natural beauty. Enter the Garajonay National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the laurel forest wraps the landscape in a magical and mysterious atmosphere. You'll visit Chipude and El Cercado, known for their pottery tradition, and have the chance to discover the Silbo Gomero, a unique whistled language recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

During the tour, you’ll enjoy the peaceful charm of small towns like Igualero, the highest village on the island, and immerse yourself in the history and culture of this Canarian jewel. You’ll also have the option to taste the island’s delicious cuisine, with typical products such as almogrote, gofio, and palm honey.

This excursion includes everything you need for a carefree experience: an official Canary Islands guide, ferry tickets, and comfortable transport in an air-conditioned bus. Just relax and let yourself be swept away by the magic of La Gomera.

Don’t miss the chance to discover this fascinating island in an exclusive and personal way. Book now and get ready for a journey you’ll never forget.

groupDetails.desc:
In Tenerife, from the highest volcano to the Seaside, on a Bike and without pedaling.The joy of the downhill biking and the beauty of the real hidden Tenerife. 22 miles touring down surfaced roads, without pedaling, in a group with a Guide and a support vehicle, at a very relaxed speed and stopping briefly to take pictures, have a drink or sample the local tapas Since 1999, we´ve shown you the real Tenerife and we do it the nicest way: on a bicycle!.

From the National Park of Mount Teide to the seaside, crossing volcanoes, forests, villages and wastelands, with beautiful views, and all of it downhill. Come with us to spend the most special day of your holidays, call us and well take care of everything from picking you up to dropping you off.When booking we will agree to a pick up point that is convenient for you and a certain time when we will collect you, generally just outside your Hotel or Apt. with a minibus.

We will then drive up to the starting point, which is very close to the base of Mount Teide, and if you have not yet seen the National Park, we will drive a little bit further ( its only a couple miles away) so that you do not miss it! Driving up to the starting point, which is 7,200 fl high, will take aprox. one and a half hours.

Once at the starting point, we will give you some printed instructions, in your language, about safety rules and the signals we will use during the trip. We will also fit you with helmet, gloves and a high visibility vest, complemented, in winter, with windbreaker jacket and / or leggings. Also with a bicycle your size, of course!.If you carry bags, rucksacks, bottles or other objects, you can, if you wish, for your comfort leave them in the support vehicle, which is always just behind the group.

We will travel at a moderate speed, keeping our group together, and we will make several stops ( every 3 miles or so) to take photos, have a drink ( hot or cold, depending on the season) or enjoy a picnic with cheese, olives, bread, water or wine in winter or, in summer, sangria and fresh fruits of the season.

ALL included in the price.While we are riding our bikes we will cross volcanic landscapes, thick pine forests, small villages where grapes and potatoes are still grown, other, almost desertic areas, and sll sorts of roads, always surfaced, till our arrival to the seaside, after some 20 or 22 miles, depending on the day. The trip down takes approximately two and a half hours. Once arrived, we will celebrate the completion of the trip with a toast of Spanish Cava and then we will drive you back to your Hotel.

On this excursion through southern Tenerife, you will discover the island's most authentic flavors and renowned wines, with the convenience of returning to your accommodation in time to continue enjoying your day.

We will start with a visit to Finca Las Margaritas, where you will learn about traditional banana cultivation and taste products made with gofio, palm honey, and tropical fruits.

groupDetails.desc:
Finca Las Margaritas is based on extensive volcanic wasteland that since 3 or 4 million years ago covered the coastal platform of Las Galletas. In this large agricultural area of 825 Ha is located the largest bananas plantations in greenhouse of Tenerife, where moves a volume of more than 26 thousand tons for export anually.

FINCA LAS MARGARITAS began with the cultivation of banana in Las Galletas in the year 1977, the union and several family members of Adolfo Guerra González entrepreneurship and Margarita Hernández Pérez, later named the estate, being 86 years old in 2012. Both came from a long family generation of farmers in S/C de La Palma and San Andrés y Sauces.

On this farm are produces 2 cultivars of Canary Island banana, the great dwarf and the thick Palm or small dwarf, the Dwarf Cavendish variety, reaching an average of 45-50 klg per bunch, and can find copies that they exceed the 70 klg. The acreage is of approximately 7 Ha with 98% of bananas and 2% of fruit trees such as: mango, papaya and avocado.

Bat4All is an exceptional and inclusive boat, designed to offer an accessible sailing experience for everyone, including people with reduced mobility. This barrier-free boat can accommodate up to 10 people and 4 wheelchairs, guaranteeing comfort and personalisation.

Start your journey in the spacious aft cockpit or relax on the comfortable bow cushions. The upper deck, with ample seating and a sun deck with artificial grass, is ideal for whale watching. The qualified crew will guide you through the nature reserve, introducing you to sea turtles, dolphins and whales. Snorkelling equipment is provided to explore beneath the surface, and when you return, a delicious cold Italian pasta awaits you.

The bathroom is wheelchair accessible and the crew offers assistance in the sea, ensuring that everyone can swim and snorkel. We will anchor in a serene bay with warm waters (20/22 degrees all year round). With a large sun deck for whale watching, relaxing and sunbathing, Bat4All is perfect for families and private events.

groupDetails.whygo: Tenerife is the largest and most populous island of the seven Canary Islands; it is also the most populated island of Spain. About five million tourists visit Tenerife each year, the most of any of the Canary Islands

groupDetails.willDo: In this excursion you will discover the essence of Tenerife in one single day. You will visit places full of culture and history.

groupDetails.name: Island Tour + Masca
groupDetails.desc:
This excursion gives you the opportunity to get to know the essence of Tenerife in just one day.

We will start the day by visiting Candelaria. This coastal town is home to the Basilica of Candelaria, one of the most important places of worship in Tenerife. On the seashore you can admire the imposing bronze statues commemorating the ancient Guanche Kings of Tenerife.

The excursion continues in the Historic-Artistic Site of La Villa de La Orotava. The cobbled streets of its historic quarter will take us to places full of charm and culture such as La Casa de Los Balcones, the Town Hall Square or the Church of Nuestra Señora de La Concepción.

We will continue our journey through the north of Tenerife until we reach Garachico, a charming coastal town, whose history is marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. We will stroll through its historic centre, declared a Site of Cultural Interest, and visit such emblematic places as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by volcanic lava, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that protected the town from pirate attacks.

Here you will have free time to have lunch on your own or taste the Canarian gastronomy in one of the restaurants we recommend.

After this visit, we will enter the Teno Rural Park where we will enjoy its impressive natural landscapes. Its winding roads will take us to Masca, a hamlet surrounded by spectacular cliffs that preserves its traditional Canarian architecture.

groupDetails.name: Teide Masca (Grand Tour)
groupDetails.desc:
On this tour we will spend a full day touring the most representative places in the north of Tenerife.

Our first visit will be to the Teide National Park, located in the heart of Tenerife and home to the highest peak in Spain: the volcano El Teide. Here we will stop for about 30 minutes to admire the impressive volcanic landscapes of Las Cañadas del Teide, not forgetting the emblematic Roques de García.

After this visit, we will descend to Icod de los Vinos where we will have the opportunity to contemplate the famous Drago Milenario, which is said to be more than 800 years old. You will have free time to have lunch on your own or enjoy the Canarian gastronomy tasting one of the menus that we recommend in some of the restaurants in the area.

The next destination is Garachico, a colourful coastal village with a history marked by a volcanic eruption in 1706. Here we will stroll through the streets of its historic quarter, recognised as a Cultural Heritage Site and one of the most representative of the Canary Islands, and discover emblematic sites such as the natural pools of El Caletón, formed by lava flows, or the Castle of San Miguel, an ancient fortress that defended the town from pirate attacks.

We will follow the route and enter the vibrant nature of the Teno Rural Park until we reach the hamlet of Masca, located between impressive valleys and ravines. Let yourself be surprised by the charm of the traditional architecture of this enclave, declared a Site of Ethnographic and Historical Interest and an Asset of Cultural Interest.

groupDetails.willDo: In the castle of Count Don Rodrigo you will witness an authentic knights equestrian tournament, while having a feast in medieval style.
groupDetails.canDesc: Free cancellation up to 48 hours before the activity. If you cancel within 48 hours of the activity, 50% will be charged.
groupDetails.name: Medieval Show
groupDetails.desc:
The San Miguel Castle is an impressive construction of 6,000 square metres and made of Canarian canto stone, with principal towers of more than 16 metres in height and an extensive area of 20,000 square metres .From the moment you enter the grounds, you find yourself in an authentic medieval world.

The entrance is decorated with historical armour, swords, chests and scrolls of the medieval epoch. The Count, Don Rodrigo, and his daughter, the young Countess, will greet you and welcome you to their Castle. The kind subjects of Count Rodrigo will guide you to the Tournament Hall, where the complex show of medieval fights and games will take placein the presence of the Counts in their Royal box seats.

During the Tournament, you will be served the banquet just as it was done in medieval times; The soup is drunk and an entire chicken per person with its garnish is eaten by hand.The dinner is completed with dessert and beverages.

The Count´s guests are seated in stands of long tables and benches where the visibility is optimal from anywhere in the Tournament Hall. The sand arena where the horses and knights will perform is of 50 metres in long.

The Hall has a capacity of 1100 guests.Usually after the Tournaments, the guests move to adjourn to a second hall which has a capacity for 800 guests.

The Ballroom, as Count Rodrigo calls it, has a large stage where the guests can dance, where any type of performance can be arranged: Orchestra, Comedians, Acrobatics, Spanish Ballet, etc.

Siam Park has been named, for the seventh consecutive year, the best water park in the world by TripAdvisor users.

A place full of different environments in which the vegetation catches you and every corner is a source of emotion, where both the little ones and the older ones will find a perfect space for the "Siam experience" to be unforgettable.

The little ones will be able to enjoy Coco Beach, a water park within the water park itself, and they will become true adventurers enjoying exciting attractions such as Bodhi Trail, Sawasdee or The Lost City, while those seeking tranquility will be able to enjoy the 13,000m2 from Siam beach, a white sand beach in the Algarve, and the birth of its waves at Wave Palace.

For adrenaline lovers, the thrill is guaranteed with Tower of Power, the impressive 28-meter high slide whose route ends under a marine exhibition with fish, rays and sharks, or Singha, the fastest water roller coaster in the world, with almost 250 meters of frenetic travel, extreme speed corners and 14 changes of direction that defy the laws of physics.

To complete the experience, the park has perfect spaces for all kinds of needs where you can unleash unknown sensations, several establishments where you can eat and recharge your batteries with a gastronomic selection where you can find a wide variety of organic dishes.

In addition, to enjoy exclusively, Siam Park has VIP Houses and private Villas equipped with all the luxury of details to make your experience unforgettable.

Discover with us the charming town of Puerto de la Cruz, located in the coastal area of the Orotava Valley, in the north of Tenerife. You will have the whole day at your leisure to enjoy a pleasant day by the sea and discover all that this town has to offer.

Despite its popularity with travellers who visit the island every year, Puerto de la Cruz has not lost its seaside charm. You can stroll through its beautiful streets and squares, such as the Plaza del Charco or the Muelle Viejo.

Many people believe that one of the most outstanding attractions of the municipality is its mild climate that is maintained throughout the year, a fact that was described by several European naturalists who visited Puerto de la Cruz in the 18th and 19th centuries.

You will have the opportunity to walk around the city and discover such emblematic places as the Botanical Gardens or the spectacular Martiánez Lake, and end the day watching the waves break on the coast of San Telmo.

groupDetails.desc:
The Yate Sofía is one of the pioneering companies offering big game fishing excursions in Tenerife, with a history dating back to 1967, when they began taking the first tourists on fishing trips and cruises in the waters of the island’s southern coast.

This vessel, a STRIKER 44, is built with robust marine-grade aluminum and features a hull specifically designed for deep-sea fishing, providing a safe, high-quality experience for fishing enthusiasts.

Yate Sofía maintains a daily communication network with the local professional fishing fleet, allowing them to track the movement of tuna in real time and head to the best fishing spots each day. The primary fishing technique used is surface trolling, ideal for catching large species such as marlin, tuna, wahoo, and mahi-mahi, among others.

Enjoy a unique fishing experience in the Canary Islands, sharing in-depth knowledge and passion for deep sea fishing in Tenerife with a professional and reliable team.

groupDetails.name: Jeep Safari Teide Masca
groupDetails.desc:
There are countless attractions on the island of Tenerife, but if we had to choose just a few, it would be the ones you will find on this excursion. Not only does it include a visit to some of the most remarkable and peculiar spots in the Teide National Park, declared a World Heritage Site, but also to a small village with very traditional and typical buildings: Masca.

On the route, which starts in Playa de las Américas, you will pass through villages as unique as Vilaflor, where for centuries they have known what it is like to live next to a dormant volcano. You will stop at viewpoints to contemplate the marvellous views of the island, we will go to the Pico Viejo volcano (inactive, with a crater of 800 metres in diameter full of colours) and you will also stroll through the little streets of Masca, a beautiful village that still preserves buildings from the 18th century. 

During the tour we will stop for lunch in a local restaurant where you can order a menu and enjoy the authentic Canarian gastronomy in the best possible place. On board of our 4x4 jeep you will discover the Cañadas del Teide National Park, which is the most visited in Spain. In addition, you will visit the most typical villages of the area. Throughout this route, which lasts 7 hours, you will witness the most peculiar corners of the island's geography, such as the village of Vilaflor, which is the highest in Spain, or Masca and its typical farmhouses. At each stop there will be a person who will inform you punctually about the places you are visiting, so you won't miss any of the exciting stories and incredible details.

Decide to discover the wild side of the island of Tenerife by Jeep!

groupDetails.desc:
In Tenerife, from the highest volcano to the Seaside, on a Bike and without pedaling.The joy of the downhill biking and the beauty of the real hidden Tenerife. 22 miles touring down surfaced roads, without pedaling, in a group with a Guide and a support vehicle, at a very relaxed speed and stopping briefly to take pictures, have a drink or sample the local tapas Since 1999, we´ve shown you the real Tenerife and we do it the nicest way: on a bicycle!.

From the National Park of Mount Teide to the seaside, crossing volcanoes, forests, villages and wastelands, with beautiful views, and all of it downhill. Come with us to spend the most special day of your holidays, call us and well take care of everything from picking you up to dropping you off.When booking we will agree to a pick up point that is convenient for you and a certain time when we will collect you, generally just outside your Hotel or Apt. with a minibus.

We will then drive up to the starting point, which is very close to the base of Mount Teide, and if you have not yet seen the National Park, we will drive a little bit further ( its only a couple miles away) so that you do not miss it! Driving up to the starting point, which is 7,200 fl high, will take aprox. one and a half hours.

Once at the starting point, we will give you some printed instructions, in your language, about safety rules and the signals we will use during the trip. We will also fit you with helmet, gloves and a high visibility vest, complemented, in winter, with windbreaker jacket and / or leggings. Also with a bicycle your size, of course!.If you carry bags, rucksacks, bottles or other objects, you can, if you wish, for your comfort leave them in the support vehicle, which is always just behind the group.

We will travel at a moderate speed, keeping our group together, and we will make several stops ( every 3 miles or so) to take photos, have a drink ( hot or cold, depending on the season) or enjoy a picnic with cheese, olives, bread, water or wine in winter or, in summer, sangria and fresh fruits of the season.

ALL included in the price.While we are riding our bikes we will cross volcanic landscapes, thick pine forests, small villages where grapes and potatoes are still grown, other, almost desertic areas, and sll sorts of roads, always surfaced, till our arrival to the seaside, after some 20 or 22 miles, depending on the day. The trip down takes approximately two and a half hours. Once arrived, we will celebrate the completion of the trip with a toast of Spanish Cava and then we will drive you back to your Hotel.

More than 90 games suspended between the tops of the pine trees, such as suspension bridges, nets, lianas and giant zip lines, are waiting for you to test your more intrepid side.
